item.title: Updates on Tri-Valley murder cases
item.description: “After reading through the case files, I’m struck at the similarities that arise in our local homicides and those in the national news. Making no judgments on the facts of these cases nor assumptions about how the legal process will play out, it’s just hard to ignore common themes like domestic violence, mental health, family troubles, intoxicated driving and more.” The post Updates on Tri-Valley murder cases appeared first on Pleasanton Weekly.

item.title: ‘Completely innocent’: Fencing coaches deny allegations of swindling immigrant instructors
item.description: The owners of a fencing training school in the Tri-Valley are speaking out through their lawyers to deny allegations from Alameda County prosecutors that they bilked prospective immigrant instructors from Eastern Europe. The post ‘Completely innocent’: Fencing coaches deny allegations of swindling immigrant instructors appeared first on Pleasanton Weekly.

item.title: New legislation mandates ‘American’ labeled wines to use only US grapes
item.description: State legislators from San Rafael and Tracy have introduced a new piece of legislation that would require wine labeled as “American” to be made exclusively from grapes grown in the United States. The post New legislation mandates ‘American’ labeled wines to use only US grapes appeared first on Pleasanton Weekly.

item.title: More than 70 state parks to offer free entry on MLK Day
item.description: More than 70 state parks in and around Bay Area will offer free vehicle entry on Martin Luther King Jr. Day, the California State Parks Foundation announced Friday. The post More than 70 state parks to offer free entry on MLK Day appeared first on Pleasanton Weekly.

item.title: Livermore school board stops morning meetings amid public ‘trust issues’
item.description: The LVJUSD board agreed last week to revise its regular meeting calendar for the remainder of the school year, axing all morning meetings in favor of hosting evening-only sessions for the sake of bolstering community trust. The post Livermore school board stops morning meetings amid public ‘trust issues’ appeared first on Pleasanton Weekly.

item.title: Former San Ramon police chief takes new role at AI startup
item.description: Weeks after his retirement from public employment, San Ramon’s former top cop is finding himself back in local police stations once again – but this time in a new capacity, as a civilian and representative for a San Francisco-based tech company. The post Former San Ramon police chief takes new role at AI startup appeared first on Pleasanton Weekly.
